body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is the ability to make things move or change. It comes in many forms: light, heat, sound, motion, electrical energy and chemical energy stored in food and fuel. Almost all energy on Earth comes from the Sun. Machines change energy from one form to another: a bulb changes electricity into light, a fan into motion and a solar panel changes light into electricity.

Sunlight, wind and flowing water are renewable; coal, petrol and gas are non-renewable and cause pollution. We save energy by switching off lights, using LED bulbs and walking or cycling for short trips.

Example

A solar panel changes…

sunlight → electricity

Answer: light energy into electrical energy

Example

Is coal renewable?

formed over millions of years

Answer: no, it is non-renewable

Common mistakes

  • Thinking electricity is a source rather than a form of energy.
  • Calling wood from forests endless.
  • Leaving chargers and TVs on.

faq.q: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy?
faq.a: Renewable sources such as sunlight and wind keep being supplied by nature; non-renewable ones such as coal and petrol will run out.

faq.q: How can we save electricity at home?
faq.a: Switch off lights and fans when not needed, use LED bulbs and star-rated appliances, and dry clothes in the sun.
